# v2.34-dev Release Notes

## Performance: shared, short-lived caching for the busy pages

The next phase of the performance work. As promised in the last release, this one
adds **short-lived caching** in front of the app's most expensive screens so they
stay fast when several people use them at once. **Nothing looks or behaves
differently** — the same pages, the same numbers — the app just avoids repeating
the same heavy work over and over.

### What changed

- **Concurrent viewers share one computation.** The dashboard, the heavier
  reports (*Training Records*, *Trained But Not Certified*, *Legacy Replacement
  Gap*, *Catalogue Health*, *Renewal Forecast*, *Program Compliance Trend*) and
  the partner-program compliance dashboards now cache their results for a few
  seconds. When ten people open the same dashboard at the same time, the database
  work happens **once** and everyone else is served the ready-made result instead
  of each re-running the full query-and-crunch pass. A burst of identical requests
  is also collapsed into a single database round-trip.

- **Always up to date after an edit or import.** The cache is scoped precisely to
  each company and view, and it is **cleared immediately** whenever the underlying
  data changes — adding or editing a training record, importing students or the
  training catalogue, or changing partner-program setup. So you never see stale
  numbers right after making a change; the very next page load reflects it.

- **Faster back/forward navigation.** These read-only report pages now tell your
  browser it may briefly reuse the last response, so stepping back and forth
  between reports feels snappier without hitting the server again.

### Notes

- **No database migration and no configuration required.** Caching is on by
  default with a 30-second lifetime.
- **New optional setting `REPORT_CACHE_TTL_MS`** lets you tune the cache lifetime
  (in milliseconds) or set it to `0` to turn caching off entirely.
- No functional changes: all report outputs, filters, exports and dashboards are
  identical to before — this release only changes how often the data is
  recomputed.

### Coming next

Further phases will move more of the number-crunching into the database (so the
browser downloads less), add pagination to the largest tables, and share caching
for reference data — again with no visible change to how the app works.
